item.text: A fixed daily routine suits people who benefit from predictability, such as those managing demanding jobs, school, caregiving, health habits, or attention difficulties. Repeating planned blocks reduces decision fatigue and protects important priorities. Substantial unplanned time is better when work is creative, exploratory, or dependent on changing opportunities, and when recovery or spontaneity matters. It allows room for reflection, unexpected conversations, and adapting to energy levels. Many people benefit most from a hybrid: schedule essential commitments and leave open space around them.
